stem: A grocery chain wants to stop discovering empty shelves only when customers complain. Leaders want store managers to see sales and stock movements as they happen so replenishment can be ordered the same day. Which business value of data does this goal illustrate?

choices.text: Lowering hardware spending, so that the chain can retire a few older servers in its head-office building
Generating real-time business insights, so that managers can act on events while they are still happening
Archiving records for later audits, so that the chain can prove what was sold once each year has closed
Standardizing store layouts, so that every outlet displays the same products in the same positions

stem: An insurer's executives are surprised that a pilot AI claims assistant gives vague and sometimes wrong answers. The assistant was built quickly, but the claims records it learns from are scattered across departments, partly outdated and inconsistently labeled. Which statement best explains the situation in terms of the role of data?

choices.text: AI replaces the need for data, so the answers should have been correct even though the records were scattered and outdated
Data volume alone decides AI quality, so adding more outdated records from other departments would fix the answers
Data fuels AI, so the quality, completeness and accessibility of the data behind a model strongly shape how good its results are
Data matters only for reporting, so the pilot's weak answers must come from the interface the claims staff use

stem: A retail bank runs an application where customers transfer money. Each transfer must be recorded immediately and correctly, and thousands of such small updates happen every minute. Separately, the finance team wants to analyze years of combined data from many systems for reports. Which pairing matches these two needs?

choices.text: A database for the transfers, and a second copy of that same database for the cross-system reporting
A data warehouse for the transfers, and a database for the cross-system reporting
A data lake for the transfers, and a database for the cross-system reporting
A database for the transfers, and a data warehouse for the cross-system reporting

stem: A streaming company collects clickstream logs, video thumbnails, support-call recordings and sensor files. Its data scientists do not yet know what questions they will ask, and they want the original raw data kept as it arrived so they can experiment with machine learning later. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: A data lake, which stores large amounts of data of all types in its native format without a predefined schema
A traditional on-premises warehouse that accepts only cleaned and structured tables from a nightly batch load
A transactional database with a fixed schema, so that every file is converted into rows before it is stored
A spreadsheet shared by the data scientists, where each file type is summarized into columns by hand

stem: A leadership team is deciding how to describe the difference between a data warehouse and a data lake to the board. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A data warehouse stores only video and images, while a data lake stores only numeric tables
A data lake and a data warehouse can never be used in the same company because their data cannot be combined
A data lake always requires every record to be fully cleaned and modeled before any data can be stored in it
A data lake can keep raw structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in its native format for analytics and ML
A data warehouse is optimized for repeatable business reporting and structured SQL analysis of cleaned data

stem: A furniture retailer wants to personalize its newsletter using the purchase history, website browsing behavior and loyalty-program sign-ups that it collects directly from its own customers. How is this data classified?

choices.text: First-party data, because the retailer collected it itself from its own customers and channels
Third-party data, because it describes people and so must come from an outside data aggregator
Public data, because anyone browsing the retailer's website could in principle see all of it
Second-party data, because it is about customers who each belong to a different retailer

stem: A hotel group and an airline agree to exchange anonymized booking data about travelers who have opted in to partner offers, so that each can design joint travel packages. From the hotel group's point of view, the data it receives from the airline is which kind?

choices.text: Third-party data, because the airline is another company and not the hotel group's customer
Second-party data, because it is the airline's own first-party data shared directly under a partnership agreement
Unstructured data, because exchanged booking data has no defined fields and cannot be analyzed by query
First-party data, because the hotel group now holds the records inside its own storage

stem: A marketing director wants to reach people who are not yet customers. The agency suggests buying an audience list of demographics and interests that a data aggregator compiled from many sources and sells to many advertisers. What kind of data is this, and what should the director weigh?

choices.text: First-party data, so the director can assume it is accurate because it is held in company records
Structured data only, so the director needs no checks because every field has a fixed meaning and format
Third-party data, so the director should weigh how accurate, consented and relevant it is, since the buyer did not collect it
Second-party data, so the director can expect it to be exclusive because only one partner supplied it

stem: A logistics company receives shipment events as JSON messages. Each message has labeled fields such as "shipmentId" and "status", but different carriers add different extra fields, and there is no single fixed table design. How is this data best described?

choices.text: Structured data, because a labeled field in a message proves that the data belongs in fixed rows and columns
Unstructured data, because anything that arrives as text messages carries no recognizable organization
Semi-structured data, because it has labels and organization but does not follow a rigid, fixed table schema
Unlabeled data, because the extra carrier fields mean that nobody tagged the data with the correct outcome

stem: A city transport authority wants to map its data supply chain. It starts with the moment a passenger taps a card on a bus reader, which creates a travel record that did not exist before. Which stage of the data supply chain is this?

choices.text: Data analysis, the point at which people or systems examine data to find patterns and answers
Data activation, the point at which insights are put to work in an action, product or process
Data processing, the point at which raw records are cleaned and transformed into a more useful form
Data genesis, the point at which data is first created or generated by an event, device or interaction

stem: A manufacturer's dashboards show inflated production counts. An investigation finds that sensor readings reach the central system correctly but include duplicates, readings in different units and missing values, and nothing fixes these before the data is stored. At which stage of the data supply chain is the gap, and what does it call for?

choices.text: Data processing, which needs cleaning, de-duplication and standardization before the data is stored and analyzed
Data collection, which needs the readings to be delayed so that they arrive less often at the central system
Data activation, which needs the dashboards redesigned so that managers see fewer production counts
Data genesis, which needs the sensors replaced so that the readings are never created in the first place

stem: A telecom company's analysts have built a model that predicts which subscribers are likely to cancel. The company now wants the call-center system to automatically show an agent a retention offer whenever a flagged subscriber phones in. Which data supply chain stage does this represent?

choices.text: Data analysis, where the model is trained and the cancellation predictions are first produced from the history
Data activation, where analytical results are fed into a business process or customer experience to drive action
Data collection, where call events are first gathered and brought in from the telephone system
Data storage, where the subscriber history is kept in a system that the analysts are able to query

stem: A bank describes its data supply chain activities. Which TWO of the following correctly pair an activity with its stage? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A customer opening a new savings account, which creates a brand-new record in the system, is data analysis
Building a dashboard of last quarter's loan trends is data collection
Loading daily branch transactions into a data warehouse for analysts to query is data storage
Cleaning mismatched date formats across the bank's regional systems is data genesis
Sending a list of high-value customers to the email platform for a targeted campaign is data activation

stem: A multinational has analysts in different countries who each keep their own copies of customer data in separate tools. They disagree on revenue totals, nobody is sure who may see personal data, and a regulator has asked how the company controls sensitive records. Which approach addresses all three problems?

choices.text: Data governance: shared standards for how data is gathered, defined, accessed, protected and used throughout its life cycle
Data deletion: removing all customer records so that no one is able to see personal data
Data hoarding: keeping every copy that each team has made, so that no team ever has to give up its own version
Data duplication: giving every analyst a private copy so that nobody depends on another team's version

stem: A company's leaders are debating whether to fund data governance, because some executives see it as only slowing teams down. Which TWO benefits of governance should the data leader cite? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A requirement that all data be stored in a single location regardless of regulations
Removal of the need for any data catalog, labeling or ownership of data
Guaranteed elimination of every security incident without any further technical controls
Safer self-service access, so more analysts can use governed data without exposing sensitive records
Trustworthy, high-quality data that reduces unreliable insights and AI answers

stem: A software company stores its analytical data in a proprietary format that only its current vendor's engine can read. Moving to a different engine would require rewriting and re-exporting years of tables. Leaders want a data platform that avoids this lock-in. Which approach reflects Google Cloud's openness?

choices.text: Keeping the proprietary format but adding another vendor's license to use as a backup in a future migration
Storing data in open table formats, such as Apache Iceberg, so that multiple engines can analyze the same data
Allowing only one approved engine for the whole company so that nobody ever needs to ask about moving
Converting all data to image files so that no analytics engine in particular is able to depend on it

stem: After acquiring two companies, a retailer finds sales data in one cloud, customer data in an on-premises system and product data in a third vendor's service. Reports need weeks of manual exports because the systems cannot share data easily. Which design principle best addresses this problem going forward?

choices.text: Standardizing on one closed ecosystem, so that every future acquisition must first rebuild its data in the vendor's format
Interoperability through open standards and connectors, so data can move and be queried across systems without manual copying
Isolation of each system, so that every department keeps strict control over its own data and rarely shares it
Printing the weekly reports from each system, so that employees can combine the results by hand

stem: A publisher's board asks why it should invest in a central data platform when editors already trust their instincts about which stories readers like. The data lead wants an argument based on identifying trends and informing strategic decisions. Which response fits?

choices.text: A central platform is valuable mainly because it prevents anyone outside the editorial team from ever viewing any readership figure
Reader data should be collected only for legal record keeping, since it cannot influence which stories the publisher chooses to commission
Editors' instincts are always more accurate than readership data, so the platform would be used mainly to store their conclusions
Analyzing reading behavior across years and topics can reveal trends, such as rising interest in a subject, so that investment decisions rest on evidence

stem: A hospital network's operations director receives a weekly dashboard showing admissions, average stay and bed occupancy by site. She asks a colleague which term describes the practice of turning this historical data into charts and reports that managers read to monitor the business. Which term is correct?

choices.text: Business intelligence, which presents historical and current data in dashboards and reports to support monitoring and decisions
Machine learning training, which adjusts a model's internal parameters until it predicts bed occupancy without any reports
Data ingestion, which moves records from source systems into storage but does not present or analyze them for managers
Generative AI, which creates new text, images or code in response to prompts written by the managers who read the reports

stem: A retailer has two requests. Team X wants a score for each customer showing the likelihood that the customer will stop buying in the next quarter, based on past behavior. Team Y wants first drafts of personalised marketing emails for each customer segment. Which pairing of AI approaches fits?

choices.text: Team X and Team Y both need predictive ML, because generative AI cannot produce text for marketing purposes
Team X needs a business intelligence dashboard to predict churn, and Team Y needs predictive ML to draft the emails
Team X needs predictive machine learning trained on past behavior, and Team Y needs generative AI that creates new text
Team X needs generative AI to write the score, and Team Y needs a rule-based system with fixed email templates

stem: A software company says its sales organisation is changing because AI agents now research each prospect, draft outreach, update the customer record and schedule follow-ups, with sellers reviewing the results. Which description best captures what makes this agentic AI different from a conventional chatbot?

choices.text: The assistant is given a goal, plans several steps, uses connected tools and business systems to act, and returns results for review
The assistant stores sales notes in a database and shows them on a dashboard that sellers must update by hand
The assistant only answers one question at a time from a fixed script and waits for the seller to do every follow-up step
The assistant is a model that is retrained each night on seller activity so that its forecasts become slightly more accurate

stem: A telecom provider introduces AI agents in customer support. The agents resolve many billing and plan-change requests end to end by using internal systems. Leaders want the productivity gain but are worried that an agent could take a wrong action on a customer account. Which approach balances value and risk best?

choices.text: Keep the agents read-only forever so that they only suggest answers, and humans make every change to every customer account
Give the agents narrow permissions, require human approval for sensitive actions, and monitor results as scope grows
Replace all human support staff with the agents at once, so that no one is needed to review exceptions
Let the agents act freely on every account in the first week, and rely on customers to report mistakes by phone

stem: A bank with decades of transaction data in BigQuery wants to build AI features. Its CIO says the main benefit of choosing Google Cloud for this plan is that AI can work where the data already lives, instead of the bank copying data between separate analytics and AI systems. Which Google Cloud AI benefit is the CIO describing?

choices.text: Best infrastructure for AI, where the benefit is chiefly the supply of custom chips for training large models
Sophisticated first-party models, where the benefit is chiefly a model that Google developed itself
An AI-ready data cloud, where analytics and AI services work directly on the data in the same platform
Pre-built agents and applications, where employees receive finished tools and the bank's data plays no role

stem: A professional-services firm wants every employee to get AI help with summarising documents, drafting messages and automating routine tasks within weeks, and it has no AI engineering team. Select TWO Google Cloud AI benefits that most directly match this goal. (Select TWO)

choices.text: A requirement to develop and train a custom foundation model first, so that the answers reflect the firm's voice
A data warehouse migration that must finish before any employee can use an AI assistant for documents
Best infrastructure for AI, which lets the firm design its own accelerator hardware layout for training
Agents grounded in enterprise data, which answer from the firm's own repositories rather than only from general knowledge
Pre-built AI agents and applications, which employees use without building models or writing code

stem: A card issuer's fraud team maintains thousands of hand-written rules such as "flag purchases over a set amount abroad". Fraudsters keep finding gaps, and each new pattern takes weeks to encode. Legitimate customers are also blocked by overly broad rules. Which business benefit of machine learning addresses these problems?

choices.text: ML makes the rules human-readable in a dashboard, so analysts can edit each of them more quickly than before
ML guarantees that fraud will no longer occur, so the fraud team and any review process can be removed
ML stores the existing rules more efficiently, so that the thousands of rules can be evaluated faster at the same accuracy as today
ML learns patterns from labelled past transactions, adapts to new behavior and reduces both missed fraud and false blocks

stem: An insurer has years of claim records in tables, plus millions of adjuster notes, accident photos and recorded calls that analysts have never been able to use because they cannot be searched with ordinary queries. Which business value does machine learning, including gen AI, add here?

choices.text: It makes the tables more accurate by deleting every record that does not contain a photo or an audio file
It removes the need to keep the original claim files and recordings, since the model can reproduce each of them exactly whenever needed
It turns the unstructured notes, photos and audio into information that can be analyzed with the structured claim data
It lets the insurer avoid defining a business question, since the model finds a useful objective on its own

stem: A bank wants to send each of its millions of customers a relevant product offer every month. Today, analysts segment customers by hand into a few groups, which is slow and treats very different customers alike. Which statement describes how ML helps the bank scale this decision?

choices.text: ML sends the offers itself without any data, because it infers customer interests from the bank's name alone
ML scores each customer's likely interest automatically, so offers can be personalised at a scale analysts cannot reach by hand
ML makes one decision for the whole customer base, which saves the cost of evaluating individual customers
ML produces a much larger number of hand-written segments, which analysts then maintain for each customer group separately

stem: A city utility wants software that computes each household's water bill. The calculation follows a published tariff table: a fixed charge plus set rates per usage band. Auditors require that identical readings always give identical bills. A consultant proposes training a machine learning model on past bills. What should a business leader conclude?

choices.text: Ordinary rules-based software fits, because the logic is known and must be exact and repeatable, so ML adds risk without value
A model is better because it will find a fairer tariff than the published table by learning the patterns found in past bills
A model should be trained on the auditors' comments, so that it learns which readings they will accept
A model is required because any calculation that touches millions of households must use machine learning

stem: A hospital's analytics team wants to train a model that predicts which patients are likely to be readmitted. They find that the allergy and medication-history fields are blank for a large share of patient records, although the values that are present look reasonable. Which data-quality dimension is the main problem?

choices.text: Timeliness, because the records were not updated within the expected time window
Completeness, because required information is missing from many records
Uniqueness, because the same patient appears more than once in the table
Validity, because the values present do not follow the required format or range

stem: A retailer's loyalty database shows 12,000 more members than the company believes it has. Analysis finds that customers who signed up in store and again online were stored as separate people, and the same person is counted several times in campaign reports. Which data-quality dimension is violated?

choices.text: Completeness, because required customer fields have no value in a large share of records
Consistency, because two different systems report different revenue totals for the same product
Uniqueness, because the same customer is recorded more than once and is counted repeatedly
Accuracy, because every record's values are wrong and no customer information can be trusted

stem: A logistics company's delivery-time model recommends routes using traffic and stock data that arrives in a nightly batch. Dispatchers complain that suggestions rely on road conditions from the previous day and miss current closures. Every value in the data is correct for the time it was recorded. Which data-quality dimension is the main issue?

choices.text: Timeliness, because the data is not recent enough for the decisions it supports
Accuracy, because the nightly values were incorrect when the system recorded them
Uniqueness, because road closures are listed again each night for each affected route
Validity, because the traffic values do not follow an accepted format or numeric range

stem: An HR analytics team loads employee records for a retention model. The data includes birth dates entered as text like "31-12-1985" in some rows and "1985/12/31" in others, and a few ages of -4 and 212. Which data-quality dimension do these defects most directly violate?

choices.text: Uniqueness, because several employees have identical birth years
Completeness, because the birth date column has no cells without a value
Timeliness, because dates from earlier years are older than recently entered ones
Validity, because values break the required date format and acceptable range

stem: A product-catalog table lists one SKU's colour as "Teal", which is an allowed value in the colour field and is spelled and formatted correctly. The physical product is actually orange, and customers return it. Which statement about this data is correct?

choices.text: It is both valid and accurate, because the data passed automatic format checks when it was loaded
It is accurate but not valid, because the value matches the product but breaks the field's allowed list
It is neither valid nor accurate, because every wrong value must also break a format or range check
It is valid but not accurate, because the value follows the field's rules yet does not match reality

stem: A manufacturer's finance report shows revenue for a product line that is higher than the figure in the sales team's database, even though both systems are fed by the same orders. The CFO's data team finds both numbers are internally well formed and current, yet they disagree. Which data-quality dimension is violated?

choices.text: Uniqueness, because each order is stored once in finance and once in sales
Consistency, because the same fact has different values in different systems
Validity, because a revenue figure cannot be read unless it follows a single numeric format
Completeness, because the finance report lacks the order rows needed to reach the sales figure

stem: A company's first AI pilot, a model to predict equipment failures, produced unreliable results. The review found sensor data with missing values, duplicated readings and conflicting units across plants. Select TWO statements that correctly explain why high-quality data is essential for AI. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Data quality matters only for reporting, because a model automatically corrects bad data during training
Data quality is the responsibility of the model vendor, so a company using managed AI services can ignore it
Models learn patterns from their training data, so errors and gaps in the data are learned and reproduced in predictions
A larger volume of poor data always outweighs the problems, because more rows give a model a clearer pattern
Investing in data quality up front raises trust in results and reduces rework and wasted effort after deployment

stem: A lender uses an ML model to approve or decline consumer loans. A declined applicant asks why, and regulators ask the lender to show that decisions are not based on improper factors. Which business benefit of explainable AI addresses these needs?

choices.text: It shows which inputs drove each decision, so the lender can justify outcomes to customers and regulators and spot bias
It increases the number of loans approved, because explained decisions are always more favorable to the applicants concerned
It removes the need for human oversight, because an explained decision is automatically a correct decision
It makes the model faster, because explanation replaces the calculation that the model would otherwise perform

stem: A health insurer is deciding whether to invest in responsible AI practices such as bias testing, transparency, privacy protection and human oversight before launching a claims-triage model. Select TWO business implications that support doing so. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Responsible AI is a purely technical setting in the model that only data scientists need to understand or own
Practices such as documentation, fairness testing and oversight help the insurer meet regulatory and audit expectations
Adopting responsible AI guarantees that the model will have no errors, so ongoing monitoring can stop at launch
Responsible AI practices remove all regulatory requirements, so legal review of the model is no longer needed
Reducing the chance of harmful or biased outcomes protects customers and the insurer's reputation and trust

stem: A pharmaceutical company's research group spends months reading papers, trial reports and internal notes before each new study. Leaders hear that agentic AI is changing research and product innovation and ask what an agent could change for this group. Which outcome is the most realistic?

choices.text: An agent only stores the papers in a shared folder, which scientists must still read themselves one document at a time
An agent replaces the scientists' judgement entirely, approving which compounds go to trials without any expert review
An agent guarantees that every hypothesis it proposes will succeed, so the group can skip laboratory validation steps
An agent gathers and summarises the relevant literature and internal data, proposes hypotheses, and scientists then evaluate them

stem: A media company trains and serves very large models and finds that its on-premises servers cannot scale, and training times slow its product plans. Which Google Cloud AI benefit answers this specific problem?

choices.text: Pre-built agents and applications, which supply finished employee tools but do not provide compute for training the company's models
A data-quality scorecard, which grades the company's tables but does not provide compute for training or serving models
Purpose-built AI infrastructure, with accelerators such as TPUs and GPUs, that can be scaled up as training and serving demand changes
Business intelligence dashboards, which present trained-model results to managers but do not provide compute for training
